technical_and_design_decisions: Flo is the web-based DSL editor for Spring Cloud Data Flow; the global options must be surfaced both in the parser/lexer and in the editor UI.

Global DSL options (timeout, pollInterval) will be defined in the grammar/parser as optional, position-independent tokens and translated to the underlying property values when generating the stream/app definition.
Spring Integration 4.2.1 upgrade is treated as a dependency bump with targeted compatibility fixes; no major refactor unless forced by deprecations.
JobLaunchingTasklet refactor will target reducing per-step overhead by reusing JobLauncher references, avoiding unnecessary job parameter regeneration, and minimizing object allocation per chunk.

SpEL inline expressions in stream definitions will be parsed using a dedicated SpelExpressionParser at module binding time, with the expression result applied to the payload consistently for both OOTB and custom modules.
YARN SPI will be extended with a new UNDEPLOYED state in the existing status enum and wired into the state machine/transition logic already used for other deploy states.

The admin artifact split will follow a Maven multi-module layout: a common admin core module and per-distro modules (e.g., admin-cdh, admin-hdp, admin-mapr) that depend on the core and on the matching hadoop-client libraries.
Test coverage enhancement will use the existing JUnit/Spring Test infrastructure; new tests will cover both the Flo DSL grammar cases and the XML/stream definition generation paths produced from it.
Documentation for job orchestration will be added to the existing reference documentation (Asciidoctor) following the established Spring docs structure, with runnable samples.

All estimates assume a single experienced developer performing design, implementation, unit testing, and self-review for each activity; CI builds and code review are included in each activity's effort.
assumptions: The existing Flo codebase, Spring Cloud Data Flow project structure, and YARN SPI implementation are already understood and available in the developer's workspace.
Java 17+ toolchain is available and configured (consistent with Spring Framework 6.0+).
Spring Integration 4.2.1 is binary-compatible with the current usage in the project aside from minor API changes.
JobLaunchingTasklet currently has working tests that can be reused as a baseline for performance regression checks.
A CI environment with the necessary Hadoop distributions available for verifying the per-distro admin modules is in place.
The 'OOTB' (out-of-the-box) modules and the custom module contract expose a uniform payload-passing interface, so a single SpEL hook is sufficient.
Documentation samples can be validated in an integration test, so no separate long-running manual verification is required.
No new external dependencies beyond Spring Integration 4.2.1 and the existing SpEL support are introduced; all changes are implementable with libraries already in the project.
Refactoring of JobLaunchingTasklet is bounded to performance characteristics; semantic/behavioral changes are out of scope unless required to fix discovered bugs.
